newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio de Janeiro releases rules to sell gas firms.
newsitem.headline: Rio de Janeiro releases rules to sell gas firms.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Rio de Janeiro has released rules for consortia to pre-qualify for the June 19 sale of natural gas distributors CEG and its Riogas unit, one of the firms said.
The CEG spokeswoman said Rio state's government planned to release May 5 draft bid specifications containing details about the separate sales of the two companies.

A final tender document to be published May 19 will give the base prices for both firms and the amount in privatization bonds that may be used in the auction at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange, she added.
CEG, with 559,000 customers, distributes 1.7 million cubic meters of natural gas daily. Revenues reached 200 million reais ($188.1 million) in 1996 with net worth totalling 150 million reais.
Rio de Janeiro state holds 65.4 percent of CEG's total capital stock while the federal government holds 34.5 percent.
Riogas distributes 700,000 cubic meters of gas daily and is controlled by CEG, which holds 75 percent of the firm. Federal oil giant Petrobras holds the remaining 25 percent.
